source_evidence.anchor: Alternative LR representation Ã = XYᵀ and orthonormality of X
source_evidence.observation: The paper represents an LR approximation as Ã = XYᵀ, with X having orthonormal columns. In the block setting, ε > 0 is the LR threshold and β is commonly a local block norm or the global matrix norm.

source_evidence.anchor: Frobenius norm convention and normwise approximation discussion
source_evidence.observation: Every unsubscripted norm in the analysis is the Frobenius norm. The page states submultiplicativity, invariance under left multiplication by an orthonormal-column matrix, and that LR approximation bounds are normwise rather than componentwise.

source_evidence.anchor: Equation (2.5), definition of γ_k, and gamma relations
source_evidence.observation: The paper assumes fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1 + δ), |δ| ≤ u, and defines γ_k = ku/(1-ku) when ku < 1. Gamma relations are explicitly allowed for non-integer indices.
A computed matrix-vector product with inner dimension b has a normwise backward representation ŵ = (A + ΔA)v with ‖ΔA‖ ≤ γ_b‖A‖.

source_evidence.anchor: Assumption 2.1 and following u safely smaller than ε convention
source_evidence.observation: For truncated-SVD LR construction, the paper ignores construction roundoff and assumes Ã_ij = A_ij + ΔA_ij with ‖ΔA_ij‖ ≤ εβ_ij. It states that this requires u to be safely smaller than ε and assumes that condition throughout the analysis.

source_evidence.anchor: Lemma 3.1 opening hypotheses and ordered computation
source_evidence.observation: Lemma 3.1 takes A ∈ ℝ^{b×b}, X,Y ∈ ℝ^{b×r}, and v ∈ ℝ^b, assumes X has orthonormal columns, Ã = XYᵀ, β > 0, and ‖A-Ã‖ ≤ εβ, and evaluates the product through z = X(Yᵀv).
With c = b + r^{3/2}, the computed ẑ satisfies ẑ = (Ã + ΔÃ)v with ‖ΔÃ‖ ≤ γ_c‖Ã‖, and therefore ẑ = (A + ΔA)v with ‖ΔA‖ ≤ γ_c‖A‖ + ε(1+γ_c)β = γ_c‖A‖ + εβ + O(uε).

source_evidence.anchor: Proof equations (3.3) and (3.4), combination, and Ã = A + E replacement
source_evidence.observation: The first computed stage has ŵ = (Y+ΔY)ᵀv and ‖ΔY‖ ≤ γ_b‖Y‖ = γ_b‖Ã‖. The second has ẑ = (X+ΔX)ŵ and ‖ΔX‖ ≤ γ_r‖X‖ = γ_r√r. Combining them gives the γ_c bound; replacing Ã by A+E with ‖E‖ ≤ εβ gives the bound relative to A.
For β = ‖A‖, the backward bound becomes ‖ΔA‖ ≤ (ε+γ_c+εγ_c)‖A‖, and the paper derives ‖ẑ-Av‖ ≤ (ε+γ_c+εγ_c)‖A‖‖v‖.

source_evidence.anchor: Interpretation of ε, γ_c, and εγ_c after Lemma 3.2
source_evidence.observation: The paper identifies truncation, floating-point, and accumulated mixed contributions, calls the mixed O(uε) contribution lower order, and says it will not always be tracked. Under u ≪ ε it interprets Lemma 3.1 as dominated by εβ and, for β = ‖A‖, as backward stable with respect to ε.
The paper explicitly says that Lemma 3.1 provides only a normwise error bound because useful componentwise bounds are unavailable for LR approximations.

binders: Fix matrix dimensions b and r and inputs A ∈ ℝ^{b×b}, X ∈ ℝ^{b×r}, Y ∈ ℝ^{b×r}, and v ∈ ℝ^b. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, Lemma 3.1 opening]

Fix β > 0. The ε appearing in Lemma 3.1 is inherited from the paper's positive LR-threshold convention rather than separately rebound in the lemma. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, Lemma 3.1 opening; PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, equation (2.4) discussion]

Let u be the unit roundoff, set c = b + r^{3/2}, and interpret γ_c as cu/(1-cu), requiring cu < 1 under the preceding gamma convention. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, equation (3.1); PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, definition of γ_k]

The quantifier order fixes v and the resulting computation before asserting perturbations ΔY, ΔX, ΔÃ, and ΔA; the source does not assert one perturbation that works simultaneously for every v. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, Lemma 3.1 and proof equations (3.3)-(3.4)]
hypotheses: X has orthonormal columns, equivalently XᵀX = I; X need not be square or unitary. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, Lemma 3.1 opening; PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, continuation of Frobenius-norm convention]
Ã is exactly the represented LR matrix XYᵀ. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, Lemma 3.1 opening]
The approximation satisfies the normwise truncation bound ‖A-Ã‖ ≤ εβ with β > 0. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, Lemma 3.1 opening]

Each floating-point matrix-vector multiplication obeys the paper's standard relative-error model and the inherited matrix-vector backward bound. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, equation (2.5) and Lemma 2.1, equation (2.6)]

The standing analysis convention is that u is safely smaller than ε; this convention supports the later dominance interpretation but is not restated inside Lemma 3.1's formal hypotheses. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, paragraph following Assumption 2.1; PDF p. 7, printed p. 957, interpretation of equation (3.2)]
conclusions: There exists a perturbation ΔÃ such that ẑ = (Ã+ΔÃ)v and ‖ΔÃ‖ ≤ γ_c‖Ã‖, where c = b+r^{3/2}. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, equation (3.1)]
There exists a combined perturbation ΔA such that ẑ = (A+ΔA)v and ‖ΔA‖ ≤ γ_c‖A‖ + ε(1+γ_c)β. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, equation (3.2)]
The source also writes the combined bound as γ_c‖A‖ + εβ + O(uε), while its exact mixed contribution in the preceding inequality is εγ_cβ. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, equation (3.2)]
In the proof, there exist stage perturbations satisfying ŵ = (Y+ΔY)ᵀv with ‖ΔY‖ ≤ γ_b‖Y‖ = γ_b‖Ã‖ and ẑ = (X+ΔX)ŵ with ‖ΔX‖ ≤ γ_r‖X‖ = γ_r√r. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, equations (3.3) and (3.4)]
The combined LR perturbation obeys ‖ΔÃ‖ ≤ (γ_b+γ_r√r+γ_bγ_r√r)‖Ã‖ ≤ γ_c‖Ã‖. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, proof immediately following equation (3.4)]
For the special choice β = ‖A‖, the bound becomes ‖ΔA‖ ≤ (ε+γ_c+εγ_c)‖A‖. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, paragraph following the proof]
For β = ‖A‖, the backward result implies the forward bound ‖ẑ-Av‖ ≤ (ε+γ_c+εγ_c)‖A‖‖v‖. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, forward-error display following the specialization]
definitions_and_conventions: Unsubscripted ‖·‖ means the Frobenius norm throughout the error analysis. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, Frobenius norm convention]
Ã denotes the represented LR approximation XYᵀ; A denotes the original exact matrix. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, Lemma 3.1 opening]
Hats distinguish computed quantities such as ŵ and ẑ from exact mathematical expressions. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, Lemma 3.1 and equations (3.3)-(3.4)]
In the proof, E = Ã-A is the truncation perturbation, so Ã = A+E and ‖E‖ ≤ εβ; the final ΔA combines E with floating-point perturbation. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, final sentence of the proof]

β is generic in Lemma 3.1. The surrounding BLR convention supplies local and global norm choices, and the lemma separately highlights β = ‖A‖. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, equation (2.4) discussion; PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, β = ‖A‖ specialization]

γ_k is the exact shorthand ku/(1-ku), not merely ku, and the paper permits non-integer gamma indices such as c. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, definition of γ_k and following relations; PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, c = b+r^{3/2}]
implicit_context: Matrix dimensions are dimension indices, and orthonormality of the r columns entails r ≤ b when r is positive; the lemma does not separately state a strict low-rank inequality r < b. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, dimensions and orthonormal-column hypothesis]

Assumption 2.1 ignores rounding errors incurred while constructing truncated-SVD LR factors; Lemma 3.1 itself only needs given factors satisfying Ã = XYᵀ and the norm bound. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, Assumption 2.1; PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, Lemma 3.1 opening]

The analysis is parameterized by unit roundoff u and does not fix IEEE double precision for Lemma 3.1. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, equation (2.5); PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, distinction between analysis and experimental setting]

The paper-wide u ≪ ε convention is used to interpret the truncation term as dominant, whereas equations (3.1)-(3.2) retain both roundoff and truncation terms. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, paragraph following Assumption 2.1; PDF p. 7, printed p. 957, interpretation of equation (3.2)]
statement.algorithm_linkage: The result is specifically for the ordered two-stage vector computation: first compute Yᵀv to obtain ŵ, then compute Xŵ to obtain ẑ. The actual arithmetic uses X, Y, and v, so its exact factorized target is Ãv; equation (3.1) is backward relative to Ã, while equation (3.2) adds the LR approximation error to become backward relative to A. This is the vector variant; the following full-matrix variant has only a forward bound. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, Section 3.1 introduction, Lemma 3.1, and equations (3.1)-(3.4)]
numerical_model: Every scalar operation is modeled by fl(x op y) = (x op y)(1+δ), |δ| ≤ u, for op ∈ {+,−,×,/}. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, equation (2.5)]
The first product has inner dimension b and contributes γ_b; the second has inner dimension r and contributes γ_r. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, equations (3.3) and (3.4)]
The exact accumulation of the two product errors is bounded using γ_b+γ_r√r+γ_bγ_r√r ≤ γ_{b+r^{3/2}}. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, proof following equation (3.4)]
Validity of γ_c inherits the condition cu < 1 from the definition γ_k = ku/(1-ku). [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, definition of γ_k; PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, definition of c]
Rounding in construction of truncated-SVD factors is excluded by the paper's standing Assumption 2.1 rather than included in ΔÃ. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, Assumption 2.1]
error_notions: Equation (3.1) is a normwise backward error for multiplication by the represented LR matrix Ã. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, equation (3.1)]

Equation (3.2) is a normwise combined backward error relative to the original matrix A, incorporating both LR truncation and floating-point multiplication errors. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, equation (3.2) and final proof sentence]
The β = ‖A‖ specialization additionally yields an absolute normwise forward error bound for ẑ-Av. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, forward-error display]
No componentwise backward or forward guarantee is claimed. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, normwise approximation discussion; PDF p. 7, printed p. 957, final paragraph]
norms: ‖M‖ = (Σ_i,j |m_ij|²)^{1/2}, the Frobenius norm. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, Frobenius norm definition]
The proof uses ‖AB‖ ≤ ‖A‖‖B‖. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, submultiplicativity statement]
For orthonormal-column X, ‖XM‖ = ‖M‖; hence ‖XYᵀ‖ = ‖Y‖ and the proof writes ‖Y‖ = ‖Ã‖. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, orthonormal-column invariance; PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, equation (3.3)]
Because X has r orthonormal columns, ‖X‖ = √r. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, equation (3.4) and following sentence]
constants_and_indexing: The bound uses c = b+r^{3/2}, with no offset or replacement by b+r. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, text between equations (3.1) and (3.2)]

γ_c means cu/(1-cu), and c may be non-integer under the paper's explicit real-index gamma convention. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, gamma definition and relations; PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, c definition]
The first-stage constant is γ_b because Yᵀv has inner dimension b; the second-stage constant is γ_r because Xŵ has inner dimension r. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, equations (3.3) and (3.4)]
The √r factor comes from the Frobenius norm of X, producing the r^{3/2} contribution inside c. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, equation (3.4) and combination immediately below it]
higher_order_terms: The exact generic mixed term is εγ_cβ inside ε(1+γ_c)β. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, equation (3.2)]
The paper abbreviates that contribution as O(uε) in the second line of equation (3.2), without displaying β or a hidden constant. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, equation (3.2)]
For β = ‖A‖, the mixed coefficient is retained explicitly as εγ_c in the exact specialized backward and forward bounds. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, displays following the proof]
The discussion calls the mixed contribution lower order and says it may be omitted later, but Lemma 3.1's exact bound includes it. [PDF p. 7, printed p. 957, three-term interpretation]
exceptional_values: The gamma expression requires cu < 1; γ_c is not covered by the stated definition at cu ≥ 1. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, definition of γ_k; PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, c definition]
Lemma 3.1 imposes no nonzero condition on v, so its unnormalized equalities and bounds do not exclude v = 0. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, Lemma 3.1 opening and equations (3.1)-(3.2)]

The special choice β = ‖A‖ conflicts with the lemma's β > 0 wording when A = 0; the source does not separately resolve that edge case. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, Lemma 3.1 opening and β = ‖A‖ specialization]
Overflow, underflow, subnormal behavior, NaNs, and infinities are not discussed; the claim is conditional on operations satisfying equation (2.5). [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, equation (2.5)]

undebatable_constraints: The theorem concerns real A ∈ ℝ^{b×b}, X,Y ∈ ℝ^{b×r}, and v ∈ ℝ^b. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, Lemma 3.1 opening]
X must have orthonormal columns and Ã must equal XYᵀ. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, Lemma 3.1 opening]
The approximation hypothesis is the Frobenius-norm inequality ‖A-Ã‖ ≤ εβ with β > 0. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, Lemma 3.1 opening; PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, norm convention]
The required algorithm is the ordered factorized evaluation X(Yᵀv), not a direct multiplication by A or Ã. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, Lemma 3.1 and proof equations (3.3)-(3.4)]
The first conclusion is ẑ = (Ã+ΔÃ)v with ‖ΔÃ‖ ≤ γ_c‖Ã‖. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, equation (3.1)]
The second conclusion is ẑ = (A+ΔA)v with ‖ΔA‖ ≤ γ_c‖A‖+ε(1+γ_c)β. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, equation (3.2)]
The constant is exactly c = b+r^{3/2}, and γ_c uses the finite expression cu/(1-cu). [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, c definition; PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, γ_k definition]

The exact combined inequality contains the mixed term εγ_cβ; it cannot be dropped merely because the source subsequently labels it lower order. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, equation (3.2); PDF p. 7, printed p. 957, three-term interpretation]
All error bounds are normwise Frobenius-norm bounds, not componentwise bounds. [PDF p. 3, printed p. 953, norm convention; PDF p. 7, printed p. 957, normwise-only statement]
The β = ‖A‖ result is a specialization, not a hypothesis of the generic form of Lemma 3.1. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, lemma statement and following specialization]
The perturbations are obtained after fixing v; the lemma does not state a single ΔA or ΔÃ valid uniformly over every right-hand side. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, Lemma 3.1 and proof]

The backward-error conclusion belongs to the vector algorithm; the following full-matrix algorithm is treated separately and receives only a forward-error bound. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, Section 3.1 introduction and final paragraph]

ambiguities.issue: The phrase u safely smaller than ε is not quantified.
ambiguities.evidence: The standing convention uses prose on PDF p. 5, printed p. 955, immediately after Assumption 2.1; PDF p. 7, printed p. 957, writes u ≪ ε when interpreting equation (3.2).
ambiguities.impact: It supports a qualitative dominance claim but supplies no numerical inequality from which γ_c‖A‖ ≤ εβ follows.

ambiguities.issue: The O(uε) notation suppresses scale information.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, equation (3.2), first gives the exact mixed term εγ_cβ and then writes O(uε); PDF p. 7, printed p. 957, calls the normalized mixed contribution εγ_c.
ambiguities.impact: A formal contract should retain ε(1+γ_c)β unless an asymptotic regime and hidden dependence on β, c, and matrix scales are supplied.

ambiguities.issue: The lemma calls the computation a product Av even though the executed expression is X(Yᵀv) = Ãv in exact arithmetic.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, Lemma 3.1 opening uses both descriptions, while equations (3.1) and (3.2) separately give backward interpretations relative to Ã and A.
ambiguities.impact: The computational contract must model the factorized Ã product and then add truncation error to relate it to A; it must not model direct arithmetic on A.

ambiguities.issue: The admissible integer range of b and r is implicit.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, gives matrix dimensions b and r and assumes orthonormal columns, but does not explicitly state 1 ≤ r ≤ b or r < b.
ambiguities.impact: A translation may infer positive dimension indices and r ≤ b from orthonormality, but strict low rank r < b is descriptive rather than a stated theorem hypothesis.

ambiguities.issue: The β = ‖A‖ specialization has an unaddressed zero-matrix edge case.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, first requires β > 0 and later sets β = ‖A‖ without adding A ≠ 0.
ambiguities.impact: Either the specialization is read with an implicit A ≠ 0 condition, or its algebraic bound is extended beyond the lemma's stated β-domain.

ambiguities.issue: The floating-point model does not specify exceptional arithmetic behavior or a named rounding mode.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, equation (2.5), states only the relative-error model with unit roundoff u.
ambiguities.impact: The result applies when that model holds; behavior involving overflow, underflow, subnormals, NaNs, or infinities is outside the explicit contract.

ambiguities.issue: The claimed dominance by εβ is qualitative and scale-dependent.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF p. 7, printed p. 957, says equation (3.2) is dominated by εβ under u ≪ ε, while the exact bound on PDF p. 6 also contains γ_c‖A‖ and c = b+r^{3/2}.
ambiguities.impact: No additional formal inequality eliminating dependence on c, ‖A‖/β, or the denominator 1-cu should be inferred from the prose.

contract_plain_english: Fix real A, X, Y, and v of the dimensions in Lemma 3.1, with X having orthonormal columns, Ã = XYᵀ, and ‖A-Ã‖ ≤ εβ for β > 0. Compute Yᵀv first and then multiply the computed intermediate by X. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, Lemma 3.1 and equations (3.3)-(3.4)] Under the standard floating-point model, with c = b+r^{3/2} and γ_c = cu/(1-cu), the computed ẑ is the exact product of v by a perturbation of Ã of relative Frobenius size at most γ_c. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 954, equation (2.5) and γ definition; PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, equation (3.1)] Combining this multiplication error with the LR truncation error gives ẑ = (A+ΔA)v and ‖ΔA‖ ≤ γ_c‖A‖+ε(1+γ_c)β. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, equation (3.2)] For β = ‖A‖ this becomes the exact coefficient ε+γ_c+εγ_c and implies the corresponding forward bound. [PDF p. 6, printed p. 956, displays following the proof] The mixed term is lower order only as an interpretation under the unquantified convention u ≪ ε, and every guarantee is normwise rather than componentwise. [PDF p. 7, printed p. 957, interpretation and normwise-only paragraph]
